associated_malware.name: UBoatRAT
associated_malware.description: UBoatRAT takes advantage of the /SetNotifyCmdLine option in BITSAdmin to ensure it stays running on a system to maintain persistence.

associated_commands.intent: Test the infected machine's internet connectivity by downloading a Google logo image.
Download a batch file from APT41 infrastructure after exploiting ManageEngine Desktop Central; it installs a Cobalt Strike BEACON loader.
Run by an LNK file embedded in a Word invoice lure: download rh72.bin with BITS at high priority, save it as file.exe in %AppData% and run it.
Create a BITS job named d1f2g34 as the first step of the persistence that UBoatRAT sets up in init.bat.
Add the local file net.exe to the job to be transferred to %temp%\sys.log, so BITS has a copy to complete.
Set BITS to run the UBoatRAT copy c:\programdata\svchost.exe when the job finishes or errors, so the malware keeps running after a reboot.
Resume the job so BITS keeps executing the malware periodically, even after the computer reboots.
First of five bitsadmin commands that the LOK implant uses to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server; it cancels any existing BITS job named pdj.
Create the BITS job pdj, part of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.
Set the pdj job to high priority, part of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.

Add the C2 URL carrying the computer name, user name and proxy IP to the job; Kaspersky says its purpose is not entirely clear but is probably to bypass a proxy in the victim network and give the C2 the victim's IP.
Resume the pdj job so the beacon is sent, the last command of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.
Upload (exfiltrate) data collected on the victim to the C2 server through a BITS upload job.
Download the legitimate AnyDesk executable onto a victim machine as a remote desktop access tool.
Deploy the Sodinokibi ransomware executable from the domain controller to remote systems.

related_CVE.description: Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). Tropic Trooper exploited it for initial execution, and its backdoor installer then used BITSAdmin to create a job that launched the DLL-hijacked sidebar.exe.

Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). Tropic Trooper exploited it alongside CVE-2017-11882, and its backdoor installer then used BITSAdmin to create a job that launched sidebar.exe.
Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central remote code execution. APT41 exploited it and used BITSAdmin to download install.bat, which installed a Cobalt Strike BEACON loader.

additional_mitigations: Consider reducing the default BITS job lifetime in Group Policy or by editing the JobInactivityTimeout and MaxDownloadTime Registry values in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\BITS.
Enforce proxies and use dedicated servers for services such as DNS and only allow those systems to communicate over respective ports/protocols instead of all systems within a network.
